_help: Read by the tutor package at import (AGENTS.md Rule 0: nothing in tutor/*.py names a path, a module, a model or a limit).

paths: relative to the vault unless said otherwise. {vault}, ~ and {module_dir} are filled at runtime. inboxes.module is a folder looked for inside EVERY module folder; inboxes.shared are extra folders (outside the vault allowed) scanned as well, skipped when absent. in_place: his own lecture files already in the vault, read where they are (never copied, moved or renamed): inside each module folder, every folder directly in it whose name matches one of in_place.folders, every file (at any depth below that folder) with one of in_place.extensions whose name (without extension) matches one of in_place.files. Week from the folder name first (match.week_dir), then the file name, then its first page.
state: where private tutor state lives, relative to the repo (memory/ is git-ignored). DENISSE_TUTOR_STATE overrides it.
modules: how a module folder name becomes a code and a title (mirrors scripts/next_lecture.json). Modules are discovered from the vault folder names; there is no list here.

match: regexes that find a week number or a module code in a folder name, a file name, or the first content_chars of a file's text. Keep capture group 1 as the number. First hit wins, folder before file name before contents.
extract: which extensions are read how. audio is off unless audio.enabled is true (faster_whisper, installed already; no download happens here).

model: config_entry names the entry in config.json 'models' (model_config.py); context comes from brain.json limits.num_ctx, DENISSE_NUM_CTX winning, the same knob the brain uses. chars_per_token and reserve_tokens size the chunks a long lecture is cut into. chunk_retries: how many more times one lecture chunk is asked after a model error (Ollama ResponseError, timeout, connection) or a reply with no JSON; retry_options[i] are Ollama options laid over the defaults on retry i+1 (the last one repeats). A chunk that still fails is skipped: the week's note is written from the chunks that worked and marked incomplete, or (every chunk failed) not written; either way the week is tried again on the next run.

prompt: what the local model is asked, per chunk. {module} {code} {week} {sources} {part} {parts} {text} are filled. It must answer with the JSON shape in prompt.schema; a reply that isn't JSON gets one retry with prompt.retry appended. bad_escape: a backslash in the reply that is the model's LaTeX, not a JSON escape (\pi, \frac, \theta, \neq: no escape, or a letter escape followed by a lowercase letter) -- doubled before parsing; a closing brace the reply stopped short of is put back (model.parse).

note: the tutor note's name, frontmatter and section templates. {module} {code} {week} {slug} {today} {outcomes_n} ... are filled. The name slug must be unique across the vault (scripts/vault_contract.py), hence the suffix.
limits: caps on what one note holds, so a long lecture gives a usable note, not a dump.

unmatched_reasons.module: no module: no module code or module name in the folder, file name or first page
unmatched_reasons.week: no week: no 'Week N' / 'Lecture N' in the folder, file name or first page
unmatched_reasons.empty: no text could be read from it
unmatched_reasons.audio_off: audio file; audio.enabled is false in tutor/tutor.json

model._structured_output: Constrain local replies using types derived from each prompt's schema example. False uses the tolerant parser alone; a server format rejection retries once without format. Shared by all tutor JSON calls; think is retained on both paths.

prompt.system: You are a careful study tutor for a university engineering module. You read lecture material and write down exactly what it teaches: nothing invented, nothing from outside the text. Equations are written in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
prompt.user:
Module: {module} ({code}), Week {week}. Material: {sources}. This is part {part} of {parts}.

From the text below, list what a student must be able to do after this lecture (learning outcomes), the key methods and equations it uses, any worked examples it contains, short self-check questions, and the topics it covers with what each one assumes you already know.

Reply with JSON of exactly this shape:
{schema}

Rules: keep every item short (one line); use only what the text says; LaTeX for every equation ($...$); leave a list empty rather than guess; no markdown outside the JSON.

TEXT:
{text}
prompt.retry: Your last reply was not valid JSON. Reply again with ONLY the JSON object, no prose, no code fences.

_help_don: name: what the study tutor is called (Chuen, 5 Nov 2026). Every deck, note line and commit message takes it from here.

don: the tutor's area in the vault, where its memory and Chuen's progress live (Chuen, 5 Nov: 'add my progress and memory back into' Obsidian). folder is relative to the vault; data is the sidecar subfolder for the JSON a note can't hold (what was read, topic maps, cards, Anki stats). paths.state (memory/tutor) is the OLD place: anything found there is copied here once, and read from there while the new copy is missing.

sources: which vault notes count as a module's material, besides everything in its folder: a note whose frontmatter keys name the module (code, slug or title), or which links to one of link_names. exclude_dirs are never walked.

cards: what is asked of each source note. kinds say how many cards of each sort and which engine writes them: local = Ollama (model.config_entry), claude = delegate.py (Chuen's Claude plan through the claude CLI, never an API key). A source note is asked again only when its text changes.

anki: one deck per module (deck), one note type (note_type). tsv: the file Chuen can import by hand. connect: AnkiConnect, used when reachable; cards are matched by their Id field, so a re-sync updates, never duplicates.
weak: how review stats become a weak topic. A topic is weak when its reviewed cards average at least lapse_rate lapses, or its mean ease is under ease_below (Anki's percent). score orders them.
learner: what Don files in the learner model (learner/), as measured beliefs with evidence; never an edit to his notes.
git: every vault write is committed through scripts/vault_git.py commit_owned, only the files written, never under never_dirs.
name: Don

{tutor} reads the KEATS material and your notes for each module, writes tutor notes and cards, and keeps track of what Anki says you keep forgetting. Its working files are in `{data}/` beside this note.

> Made from the notes linked under each heading. Anki deck: `{deck}`.
don.cards_held_intro: Cards held back by the check, including cards about another module. They are not sent to Anki.

scope._help: Topic ownership is discovered from module folders, their topic maps and source-note topic metadata. Match full names ignoring case and whitespace; do not infer ownership from links or word overlap. A name shared with the current module is eligible, but the checker must still judge its use in the source. The scope fingerprint invalidates checks when ownership or policy changes.
scope.rule: Stay within {module}. Its topic map and its notes define what it teaches; the map may be incomplete. Other modules may share mathematical tools: keep a shared tool when the NOTE actually explains or applies it inside {module}. A link, heading or one-line cross-reference to another module is navigation, not teaching or evidence for a card. Do not turn it into a question about that other module. Judge the front and back as well as the topic label: relabelling a foreign fact does not make it part of this module. Use only substantive teaching in the NOTE; an empty cards list is better than cards inferred from links.

recall.describe: recall cards: a definition, a named result or an equation to state from memory; the front is a full question that says what to give, never just a name

method.describe: method cards: given a situation, which method to use and why

problem.describe: short worked problems: a small problem on the front, the worked answer in a few steps on the back

tutorial.describe: tutorial problems written like the module's problem-class sheets (STYLE below): a physical set-up with its given quantities and symbols, then numbered parts (i), (ii), (iii) that build up (derive, then calculate, then interpret). Write NEW problems: set-ups and numbers may be new, but every law, equation and method must be one the note uses. The back is a full worked solution laid out like a walkthrough, each label on its own line: 'Set-up:' (axes, assumptions), then '(i)', '(ii)'... each with short working and its key equation in \\[ \\] on one line, then 'Answer:' with every final result and its units, then 'Check:' with one sanity check (limits, units or direction). Never point to the note by number (eq. (9), Figure 2): he sees the card without the note, so name the law or write the equation out
tutorial.check_note: [new problem: its numbers are not in the note. Judge whether the physics, every step and every number in the worked solution are correct, and whether the method is one the note uses.]

cards.system: You are {tutor}, a careful study tutor writing Anki cards for a university engineering student. Use only what the note says; nothing invented. Equations in LaTeX between \( and \). Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.

check.system: You are {tutor}, checking Anki cards before a university engineering student drills them. A wrong card teaches him a wrong fact, so be strict, as a professional examiner would be. A card is right only if (1) the physics or maths on it is correct, (2) the back actually answers the front, specifically and not vaguely, and (3) it agrees with the source note, (4) the front is a complete question a student could answer, not just a name or a heading, and (5) it teaches this module, with substantive support in the source rather than a link or mention of a different module. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.

reasons.no_verdict: not checked: the checker gave no verdict for this card
reasons.unreachable: not checked: the checker ({engine}) did not answer ({why})
reasons.no_fix: wrong, and the note gives no corrected answer: {reason}
reasons.fix_unsupported: wrong; the correction offered is not backed by the note: {reason}

style._help: Kinds with style: true get the module's own problem-class sheet as a style example. globs are relative to the module folder; {week_dir} is the note's week folder; first readable hit wins.
style.text:
STYLE: the module's own problem-class sheet ({name}). Match its format, difficulty and wording; write new problems from the NOTE, never copy these:
{style}

math._help: tutor/mathfmt.py. delimited: [kind, regex with a 'body' group, optional reject-body regex], earliest accepted span wins; config order breaks ties (display first). Single dollars cannot close before a digit or another dollar; a number followed by prose words or punctuation and whitespace is treated as currency. Numeric equations and padded maths remain valid; escaped dollars stay in the body. adjacent_separator keeps neighbouring maths spans from forming ambiguous target delimiters. bare: 'token' splits prose, 'braces' groups balanced arguments; a token with 'sign' starts maths, 'operator'/'operand' tokens around it join it, 'trailing' punctuation is left outside. targets: the delimiters each place renders.

_help_consult: consult (part 5, tutor/consult.py): the tutor as the specialist every other agent asks first about Chuen's modules, coursework, revision or learning (Chuen, 5 Nov 2026: 'treat Don like a professional opinion on task'). python -m tutor consult "<question>" [--module X] [--json]; the agent hub's ask_don, the Orchestra runner (orchestra/consult.json) and Denisse's tutor_consult all call it.

The answer is grounded only in vault notes: every note of the module (sources.py: the tutor notes, his own, anything tagged or linked) scored by how many of the question's content words it holds (topics.stop_words / match_min_word_chars apply), the tutor notes of the weeks whose topic-map entry names those words boosted by week_boost. The top max_notes notes with at least min_overlap_words go to the model. No note at all: no model call, answer = no_notes, confidence low.

confidence: from how much of the question the chosen notes cover (coverage = words found / words asked). high needs high_share and high_min_notes notes, medium needs medium_share, else low; a model that says it was not confident drops one level when downgrade_when_not_confident. sources are the notes given to the model, as vault links; the model never names a source itself.

engines (cards.engines names): the local model first; a question on a hard topic (teach.hard_topics) goes to the hard engine at once; a local answer that is empty or not confident goes to the fallback engine, waited for (a consult is synchronous). delegate.DRY_RUN, or a fallback that fails, keeps the local answer and says so in caveats.

Every consult is recorded in the Don area: sidecar consults.json (last keep) and the readable note note_file, newest first, committed with git.messages.consult. who: the engine that answered (who_labels), or who_none.

consult.system: You are {tutor}, the study tutor for a university engineering student, giving a professional opinion to another assistant that is working on something about his modules. Answer only from the notes given: his lecture notes as the tutor wrote them up, and his own notes. Where the notes do not cover something, say so under caveats rather than filling it in from general knowledge. Equations in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
consult.schema: {"answer": "the opinion, a short paragraph or a few bullet lines", "caveats": ["what the notes don't cover"], "confident": true}
consult._notes_only: python -m tutor consult --notes-only: the quick opinion with no model call at all (from_notes). Orchestra uses it when the GPU is busy or the model consult failed. The chosen notes' lines that hold the question's words, at most max_lines per note, each note's excerpt capped at excerpt_chars, one line per note joined by sep. who names it in the result; confidence drops one level (no model weighed it).

notes_only.caveat: Quick answer from his notes only: no model read them (the local model was busy or failed), so these are the matching lines, not an opinion.

consult.no_notes: Nothing in the vault covers this{module}: no tutor note or note of his names its terms, so {tutor} has no grounded opinion to give.
consult.no_module: No module called '{text}' in the vault; the modules are: {modules}.
consult.caveat_no_notes: No notes found for the question: this is not grounded in his material.
consult.caveat_not_confident: The model said the notes were too thin to answer from with confidence.
consult.caveat_engine_failed: The {engine} engine gave no usable answer ({why}).
consult.caveat_fallback_off: A better answer needs {engine}, but hand-offs are off in this run; this is the local model's answer.
consult.caveat_fallback_failed: {engine} could not answer ({why}); this is the local model's answer.
note_front: description: "What the other assistants asked {tutor} about Chuen's modules, and the opinion {tutor} gave from his notes, with its confidence and sources. Regenerated by python -m tutor consult; edit a copy, not this."
> Each opinion was given from the notes linked under it, to another assistant working on his study. Advisory: a subject expert's view, never an override. Newest first.
hub_line: What the other assistants asked {tutor}: [[{stem}]] (`python -m tutor consult`).

_help_teach: teach (part 3): explaining a topic. The material is the topic map entry, the tutor notes of the weeks it names and his own notes that mention it (sources.py), capped to material_share of the model's chunk. learner_areas are the learner-model areas quoted to the model (how he likes to be taught). engines name cards.engines entries: local = Ollama, hard/fallback = delegate.py (Claude). hard_topics: topic words Chuen marks as hard, always Claude. self_check: what a local answer must have to stand; one that fails goes to the fallback engine in the background (BACKGROUND in chat.py), the local answer given meanwhile.

quiz: the short check from the cards (part 2). questions is the default count, also the end-of-round check study mode offers (study_mode.set_round_end). order: which cards first -- weak and due come from the Anki stats. mark_engine marks his answers against the card backs.

exam: longer problems in the style of the coursework and past papers found in the module folder (paper_globs, relative to it; PDFs and Office files read by extract.py). engine writes the question and a mark scheme; marking_engine marks his answer against it, step by step. The open question and the history live in practice_file.

chat: every sentence the chat tools (tutor/chat.py, registered in tools.py) return to the model. intro is the first sentence of every result, so a reply that leaves the tutor out still gets it (tool_policy.json reply_must_mention). In quiz and exam, what follows ' Tell him' is for the model only: brain.json honesty.result_cut_markers cuts it off when the result itself is shown (must_mention_replaces), so he sees the questions and not the instructions. {tutor} is the name above.

teach.learner_none: - nothing known yet; teach plainly, one step at a time
teach.system: You are {tutor}, a patient study tutor for a university engineering student. Teach from the material given: his lecture notes and his own notes. Say when the material does not cover something rather than inventing it. Equations in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
teach.schema: {"summary": "one line: what the topic is for", "steps": ["..."], "question": "...", "answer": "...", "confident": true}
lessons_front: description: "{code} {module}: every topic {tutor} explained in chat, step by step, with the check question. Regenerated by the tutor tools; edit a copy, not this."
> Each lesson was taught from the notes linked under it ({tutor}'s tutor notes and your own). Newest first.
teach.lessons_none: - Nothing explained yet: ask {tutor} to explain a topic in chat.

quiz.mark_system: You are {tutor}, marking a student's short answers against the answers on his revision cards. Be fair: the same idea in other words is right; a missing key part is wrong. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
quiz.offer: Round {round} done: {tutor} can give a {n}-question check on what he has been studying -- offer it, and quiz him if he says yes.

exam.system: You are {tutor}, setting an exam-style problem for a university engineering student, in the style of his module's coursework and past papers. Use only the material given for the content. Equations in LaTeX between $ signs. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
exam.style_none: (no coursework or past paper found: set a standard multi-part problem)

exam.mark_system: You are {tutor}, marking a university engineering student's answer to an exam-style problem against its mark scheme. Mark each step of the scheme: say what he earned and why, in a sentence he can act on. Be strict on method, lenient on arithmetic slips that carry through. Answer with one JSON object and nothing else.
exam.mark_schema: {"marks": 12, "total": 20, "steps": [{"step": "...", "awarded": 2, "of": 4, "comment": "..."}], "feedback": "two or three sentences: what to revise"}

exam.entry_open_line: Answer it in chat and {tutor} will mark it.

chat.no_module: {intro} I don't know a module called '{text}'. The modules in the vault are: {modules}.

chat.says: {tutor} says this with {confidence} confidence, from {n} note(s) of his; relay it as {tutor}'s view, with the confidence, and keep your own view separate.
chat.consult_empty: {intro} There was no question to put to {tutor}. Ask him what he wants {tutor}'s opinion on.
chat.from_claude: explained by Claude from the lecture notes
chat.escalated: {intro} {why} so {tutor} has asked Claude for a proper explanation of {topic} ({module}); it will pop up here when it's done and go into {note}. Tell him that.
chat.why_hard: {topic} is marked as a hard topic,
chat.why_check: the local model's explanation didn't pass {tutor}'s own check,
chat.why_dry: {topic} needs Claude, but hand-offs are off in this run,
chat.no_cards: {intro} No cards for {module} yet, so nothing to quiz from. Make them with: python -m tutor cards {module}
chat.no_stats: {intro} No Anki review stats for {module} yet, so nothing is measured as weak. He needs to review the cards in Anki and run: python -m tutor anki-sync

chat.weak_none: {intro} Nothing measured as weak in {module}: {cards} card(s), {reviewed} reviewed, no topic lapsing (synced {date}).{learner}

chat.no_open: {intro} There's no open question for {module} to mark. Give him an exam question or a quiz first.
chat.marking: {intro} {tutor} has sent his answer to Claude for marking against the mark scheme; the marks and step-by-step feedback will pop up here and go into {note}. Tell him that.
chat.mark_failed: {intro} Couldn't mark that: {why}. His answer is kept; try again later.
chat.model_failed: {intro} The model didn't give a usable {what}: {why}. Say so; don't make one up.

_help_progress: progress (part 4, tutor/progress.py): python -m tutor progress [module]. Per module: lecture weeks on KEATS (the ingest state, plus inbox files downloaded since, placed by folder and file name only) against weeks with a tutor note; the topic map with each topic's Anki numbers and mastery; weak topics; coursework notes (paths.coursework_globs) with due date and items left; what to study next.

note: the vault overview, relative to the vault. Only the text between block_start and block_end is regenerated; everything outside it is his and kept (the frontmatter's updated: line is the one thing changed). front is used only when the note doesn't exist yet.

module_file: the full record per module in the Don data folder (study_brief.py reads its weak topics). dataset_file: one row per module, the Atrium hub's study table (atrium/snapshot.py copies it to the hub as study.json).
mastery: reviewed share of a topic's cards x (1 - lapses per reviewed card / lapse_rate_zero), floored at 0, as a percent. None until something is reviewed.

next.order: which kinds of next step come first. ingest = lectures on KEATS not read yet; weak_coursework = a weak topic that a coursework item due soonest needs; weak = other weak topics; deadline = coursework due within horizon_days with items left; due = Anki cards due; unreviewed = topics with cards never reviewed; uncarded = topics with no cards. max caps the list.

progress.name: study-progress
front: description: "Study progress across every module, kept by {tutor}: lectures read against KEATS, topics and Anki mastery, weak topics, coursework deadlines and what to study next. The block between the markers is regenerated by python -m tutor progress; write your own notes outside it."
block_intro: > From the KEATS inbox, the tutor notes, the Anki review stats and your coursework notes. This block is regenerated by `python -m tutor progress`; anything you write outside it stays.
progress.none: - Nothing to report yet: put the KEATS files in the inbox and run `python -m tutor ingest`.

overview_head: | Module | Lectures read | Topics | Mastery % | Weak | Next deadline |
topics_head: | Topic | Weeks | Cards | Reviewed | Lapses | Mastery % | Weak |

progress.lectures: - **Lectures:** {n} of {on_keats} on KEATS read into tutor notes (week(s) {read}).
progress.lectures_new: - {n} file(s) in the inbox since the last `python -m tutor ingest`.
progress.coursework_undated: - **Coursework:** {coursework}, no due date found: {left} of {total} item(s) left.
progress.coursework_none: - **Coursework:** no coursework note in the module folder.
progress.practice: - **Practice with {tutor}:** {exams} exam question(s) marked ({mean}% on average), {quizzes} quiz(zes).
progress.topics_none: - No topics yet: `python -m tutor ingest`, then `python -m tutor cards {module}`.
progress.next_none: - Nothing pressing: keep up the Anki reviews.

next.ingest: Read the new lectures: week(s) {weeks} are on KEATS without a tutor note -- run `python -m tutor ingest`.
next.weak_coursework: Revise **{topic}** ({links}) before {coursework} is due {due} (in {days} days): Anki says it keeps lapsing.
next.weak: Revise **{topic}** ({links}): Anki says it keeps lapsing.
next.deadline: {n} of {total} item(s) left in {coursework}, due {due} (in {days} days).
next.due: Review the {n} card(s) due in Anki, then `python -m tutor anki-sync`.
next.unreviewed: Start reviewing {n} topic(s) never reviewed in Anki: {topics}.
next.uncarded: Make cards for {n} topic(s) with none: {topics} -- `python -m tutor cards {module}`.
